- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative or neutral (≤0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to align with mean-reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days; apply a 1–3% downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- If model shows strong upward trend (e.g., 3+ consecutive rising forecasts) with low sentiment, reduce forecast slope to reflect mean reversion.
- If true outcome deviates >3% from model in first 3–5 days, adjust forecast for next 7–10 days by averaging recent 3-day true values to reduce lag error.
- When sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-period, model often fails to catch momentum; apply a 1–2% upward adjustment starting from day of sentiment shift.
